transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Dr Ana (Cerebra CTO), Mark (Infra), Jenna (Security), Oscar (ML Platform), Sasha (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): POC scope: private connectivity, egress policy, benchmark plan, success criteria (p95 latency < 250ms, throughput 300 rps steady, <5% error), timeline for pilot in mid-December. Action items: share security docs, prepare benchmark scripts, customer to share perf profile.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we've got about an hour, want to make sure we line on success criteria and the network constraints.
[00:18] Dr. Ana: great, thanks, Maya. quick background — we run inference for multimodal clinical notes and some unstructured imaging metadata. regulatory requires all inference to stay in eu-west-1 region and no outgoing egress except approved endpoints.
[00:36] Maya: understood. that's the residency constraint. Mark, can you add anything on infra side?
[00:42] Mark: yeah, we're on AWS, we prefer VPC peering to a dedicated account but open to AWS PrivateLink for tighter control. main ask: no NAT egress to internet, outbound only to our S3 gateway and an internal audit collector.
[00:58] Liam: okay, technically we can support both. VPC peering is lower complexity but depends on route tables and CIDR overlap; PrivateLink gives you endpoint-level control and prevents route table leaks but requires an endpoint service.
[01:15] Jenna: security note — we'll need KMS integration on the private deployment side, and audit logs forwarded to our Splunk. SOC2 evidence and key rotation policy are must-haves.
[01:30] Priya: we can integrate KMS, we also have a feature for customer-managed keys in the Private offering. we'll include HSM notes.
[01:40] Sasha: timeline — we need a 2-week pilot to validate latency and cost. can we do benching next week?
[01:46] Maya: yes, propose a 2-day benchmark window where we run baseline + load ramp and a tail-latency profile.
[01:52] Oscar: what exactly will you measure? p95, p99?
[01:56] Liam: we'll collect p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, and error rates. also KV cache hit rates if you plan persistent sessions; that affects latency.
[02:10] Dr. Ana: success criteria: p95 < 250ms for typical prompts, cost per 1k tokens below our threshold (we'll share), and no egress outside the approved list.
[02:23] Maya: good. we'll codify that in the SOW. also need to confirm concurrency and average seq length. Mark?
[02:30] Mark: current production pattern is ~300 rps sustained, spikes to 1.2k qps for 30s, avg seq len ~120 tokens, majority are chat-style back-and-forth so KV cache helps.
[02:46] Liam: ok that's helpful — with that pattern we'll recommend dynamic batching tuned for latency SLOs and an autoscale profile in Dedicated or Private.
[02:56] Jenna: about egress: we cannot allow any outbound except to our internal S3 endpoint (vpce-xyz), Splunk collector (10.10.5.12), and our internal license server. everything else is blocked.
[03:10] Maya: that's fine — we'll set up a PrivateLink endpoint for ingestion and an S3 gateway in the same region. we'll document the exact IPs and service names.
[03:20] Dr. Ana: what about log retention and redaction? can you stream audit logs without sending model inputs?
[03:27] Priya: yes, logs can be configured to omit prompt text; we can send telemetry metadata + hashes.
[03:34] Liam: during benchmarks we usually enable verbose logs to capture errors, but you'll control retention and redaction in the config.
[03:40] Sasha: benchmarks — please specify what you'll need from us to run an apples-to-apples test.
[03:45] Liam: sample prompts, traffic shape (qps timeline), target concurrency, allowed egress endpoints, and an S3 bucket for artifacts. we'll provide a JMeter-style template and a small harness that reads from your prompt set.
[03:58] Mark: will the benchmark consume our credits or yours? who pays for the compute?
[04:03] Maya: Redwood will cover initial bench compute for two days, anything beyond we can discuss credits or trial terms.
[04:10] Dr. Ana: good. on private connectivity, are there tradeoffs between peering and PrivateLink in latency or cost?
[04:18] Liam: peering can be slightly lower latency, but PrivateLink reduces blast-radius and is more straightforward for strict egress because endpoints are explicit. cost depends on cross-account data transfer and endpoint pricing; we'll quantify both in the bench report.
[04:31] Jenna: also worth mentioning we need RBAC mapping to our IdP — SAML SSO for user access and RBAC at token-level so only certain teams can see raw prompts.
[04:43] Priya: we support SAML SSO, org-level RBAC, and token-level scopes. we'll include a mapping guide.
[04:50] Oscar: curious about quantization — can you support int8 for our models to reduce GPU memory?
[04:55] Liam: yes, the runtime supports quantized variants and we can serve a quantized model in Private. we'll list the supported quant formats and the expected perf/cost tradeoffs.
[05:05] Maya: devops question — we need to keep the entire inference path in eu-west-1. can Redwood pin deploys to regions?
[05:12] Priya: yes, we can pin model deployments to a region and have smart routing fallback disabled for the POC.
[05:18] Sasha: great. on success criteria again: if p95 is 260ms, are you still okay? is there a bucket for tolerances?
[05:25] Liam: we'll treat the 250ms p95 as target with a 10% buffer for short period; acceptance will be a p95 <= 275ms for the 2-day run, but we'll highlight regression vs baseline.
[05:36] Dr. Ana: that's reasonable. also SLA — we need an uptime SLA for the pilot?
[05:41] Maya: for the pilot we'll provide operational support and 99% availability for test windows; production SLA can be discussed with Dedicated contracts.
[05:48] Mark: on networking — we have overlapping CIDRs with some partner accounts; if peering collides, we'll favor PrivateLink.
[05:55] Priya: we'll include a flow for CIDR checks and recommend NAT-less design.
[06:00] Jenna: compliance question: will Redwood provide an audit trail of who called what and the prompt hashes?
[06:08] Liam: yes, we export audit logs with caller identity, model version, and request hash.
[06:15] Dr. Ana: bench metrics — besides latency, we'd like model output quality checks. how are you handling quality regression detection?
[06:23] Maya: Redwood Optimize has eval hooks; for the POC we can run a small set of golden prompts and compare outputs for regressions; if using model variants for quantization we'll compare BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and human spot checks.
[06:37] Oscar: we'll provide a 200 prompt validation set.
[06:40] Liam: perfect. that will let us measure both perf and quality tradeoffs.
[06:46] Sasha: how long to spin up a Private deployment once we sign?
[06:50] Priya: for Private with VPC peering usually 2-4 business days for infra provisioning + endpoint setup, PrivateLink similar but needs endpoint service creation which can add a day if approvals are slow.
[07:02] Mark: do you support customer-installed agents on our k8s in case we want on-prem?
[07:07] Priya: we have an on-prem package but it's a heavier lift — for this POC we recommend Private in cloud.
[07:14] Dr. Ana: cost model — what's the billing granularity?
[07:17] Maya: per-token for hosted paths, for Dedicated/Private we do reserved capacity pricing with monthly commit and overage priced per-token/throughput; we'll share an estimate based on your traffic.
[07:30] Jenna: encryption in transit — need mTLS between our VPC and the endpoint.
[07:35] Liam: supported. PrivateLink also terminates TLS on the endpoint and we can require client certs.
[07:41] Maya: okay, to recap real quick: 1) Redwood to share SOC2 snippets, KMS/HSM notes, and VPC/PrivateLink architecture diagram. 2) Customer to share traffic profile, allowed egress endpoints, and prompt set by 2025-12-05. 3) Redwood to run a 2-day benchmark on 2025-12-10/11 and cover compute for that window. 4) Action items assigned. sound right?
[08:02] Dr. Ana: yes.
[08:05] Mark: yes.
[08:07] Jenna: yes.
[08:10] Maya: cool. I'll send a calendar invite for the benchmark window and permission request for the VPC peering test account.
[08:16] Liam: final technical note — during the bench we'll run with cache warm-up stage, a steady-state, and spike stage to simulate your incidents. we'll provide scripts and the perf schema.
[08:26] Oscar: quick Q — do you support tag-based cost allocation to our billing?
[08:30] Priya: yes, we emit tags and cost exports you can map in your billing tools.
[08:35] Sasha: anything else on legal or procurement we should know?
[08:38] Maya: procurement typically needs DPA + SOC2 attestation; we'll attach a templated NDA/DPA for signature.
[08:45] Dr. Ana: ok thanks, that covers it. we'll get the profile over and look for the security pack.
[08:50] Maya: thanks everyone — follow-ups in the next 24 hours.

(Transcript notes: occasional speaker ID errors, some words auto-transcribed incorrectly — e.g., "PrivateLink" appeared as "private link" once, and "KV cache" as "k v cache" in places.)
